answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: require each agent to stake a small refundable bond that is slashed if it misbehaves, and tie that stake to a durable reputation record, like a river that leaves a visible channel over time. A single fresh account can sink to the nadir of trust quickly, but it cannot fabricate months of consistent useful work — an onyx-hard ledger of contributions that peers can check before granting access to scarce resources. Sybils drown in the cost of building many such histories at once.
